title: Surface Retry-After + Redwood overload error codes in Python SDK errors
author: Monica Patel
description:
Context: Hosted overload protection is rolling out circuit breakers + load shedding. During overload we will return deterministic 429/503 with Redwood-specific error codes and a Retry-After header. Today the Python SDK raises a generic APIError and drops Retry-After and Redwood codes, which makes it hard for customers to implement correct backoff/jitter and avoid retry storms.

This PR plumbs overload metadata through the Python SDK error types: (1) parses and exposes Retry-After as both raw header value and a normalized retry_after_seconds; (2) surfaces Redwood overload error codes on exceptions (works for both Redwood REST endpoints and OpenAI-compat endpoints); (3) adds docs + examples for safe retry/backoff patterns; (4) adds unit tests covering parsing and backward compatibility.

Customer impact: clients can implement customer-actionable retries (respect Retry-After, cap max retries, add jitter) and can branch on overload codes (e.g., breaker-open vs queue-full) for better fallbacks.

What changed: - Added RedwoodErrorCode enum (subset focused on overload) and attached it to APIError via error_code (optional). - Added retry_after (raw header) and retry_after_seconds (int | None) to APIError. - Updated error parsing to read: Retry-After, x-redwood-error-code (preferred), and OpenAI-style error.code when present (OpenAI-compat mapping). - Added helper predicates: is_overload_error(), is_retryable(), and suggested_retry_delay_seconds(default=0) that prefers Retry-After when provided.

Compatibility notes: - No automatic retries were introduced. - Existing exception classes and message formatting remain unchanged except for additional attributes. - If headers are missing/unparseable, new fields are None and behavior is unchanged.

Docs: Added a new docs page ("Handling overload errors") and updated the "Errors" section to include Retry-After handling and exponential backoff with jitter. Included a small snippet for streaming disconnects (treat as retryable only if request is idempotent and you bound retries).

Testing: Added unit tests for: parsing Retry-After (seconds + HTTP-date), mapping header error codes, OpenAI-compat error object mapping, and ensuring existing error text does not change. Tests run under py3.9-3.12.

Follow-ups: We should mirror the helper predicates in TS/Go SDKs (tracked separately) and consider exposing request_id consistently (some endpoints use x-request-id vs x-redwood-request-id).
commits: sdk/errors: add retry_after + error_code fields to APIError
openai_compat: map OpenAI error.code to RedwoodErrorCode when possible
docs: add overload errors + retry guidance page
tests: add coverage for Retry-After parsing + overload code mapping
conversation: Monica Patel (2025-12-08): Implemented plumbing for Retry-After + overload codes. Main concern is keeping compatibility with existing customers who match on exception messages; I avoided changing __str__ output and only added attributes.

Ibrahim Khan (2025-12-09): Can we make Retry-After parsing robust for HTTP-date? Some proxies send a date instead of delta-seconds. Also, please ensure we don't treat malformed values as 0 seconds (that will cause tight loops).
Monica Patel (2025-12-09): Good call. I added date parsing via email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime; if parsing fails we leave retry_after_seconds=None. Also added tests for both formats.

Brian Murphy (2025-12-10): For OpenAI-compat endpoints, the error schema might have code nested under error.code but sometimes providers put it in error.type. Are we only mapping from error.code? Also, what's the canonical header name for Redwood codes?

Monica Patel (2025-12-10): Canonical is x-redwood-error-code (matches ADR). For OpenAI-compat mapping: we look at error.code first; if absent we do not guess from error.type (too ambiguous across vendors). We still include the raw OpenAI error object in the message as before.

Henry Cho (2025-12-10): Docs request: please explicitly recommend exponential backoff with jitter and honoring Retry-After; also call out that overload responses are not billed. (Support has confusion per SUP-3961.)

Monica Patel (2025-12-10): Added docs section "Billing + quotas" stating overload-protected errors are not billed for tokens (consistent with support guidance). Linked to the public docs section being updated by DevEx.
Ibrahim Khan (2025-12-11): One more: please add a helper to compute a suggested sleep time with jitter. Even if we don't auto-retry, customers will copy/paste. We should make the "safe" path easy.

Monica Patel (2025-12-11): Added suggested_retry_delay_seconds() which returns Retry-After when present else caller-provided fallback. Docs snippet uses exponential backoff with full jitter capped at 30s and respects Retry-After.
Brian Murphy (2025-12-11): Looks good. Minor nit: please include the raw header value in the exception attributes so logs can show what we received.
Monica Patel (2025-12-11): Done (retry_after: Optional[str] + retry_after_seconds: Optional[int]).
Ibrahim Khan (2025-12-12): Approved. Tests look solid and no behavior change in string formatting.
Henry Cho (2025-12-12): Approved; docs language matches the product messaging.
release_notes:
- Python SDK errors now expose retry_after/retry_after_seconds when the API returns Retry-After.
- Python SDK errors now expose Redwood overload error codes (when provided via headers or OpenAI-compat error.code).
- Added docs + examples for safe retry/backoff with jitter; no automatic retries were introduced.
